Tips & Templates

WSU Hedgerow Site

The Hedgerow Planner helps you turn a plant list into a to-scale hedgerow plan in just a few steps: create a grid, add plants, arrange them as spacing circles, then save or export (with additional view options). It runs in any web browser, needs no account, and saves your work in that browser as you go.

Getting around the screen

The planner has two areas: a panel on the left for choosing plants and saving work, and the block plan on the right where you arrange them.

  • Left panel: Add a plant (your plant menu), Selected circle (appears when you click a circle), and Saved layouts.
  • Toolbar above the plan: Layers, the View toggle, Block plan size, More options, Undo, Redo and Clear all.
  • Block plan: a to-scale grid in feet. Thin lines mark each foot; darker lines mark every 5 feet.

New to hedgerows? Check out the How To Space Plants tab in this window, or read up on all the details of Hedgerows in the guide on the WSU Hedgerows Site.

Step 1: Set the block plan size

Type the width and length of your planting area, in feet, into Block plan size. The default is 20 × 15 ft. Plan one block at a time; a long hedgerow is usually a repeating block. When planting hedgerows, we usually design on a grid of 5'x5' (the default darker lines) and plant flags at the line intersections to be able to better visualize the planting plan in real life.

Use Zoom or Fit to panel to see the whole block on your screen. Zooming doesn't change the plan's scale.

Step 2: Add plants to your menu

Your plant menu, under Add a plant, holds the plants you'll use. Fill it in one of three ways.

  1. Presets — pick from 75 plants recommended by the Native Plant Salvage Foundation. Browse them By layer (trees, large shrubs, small shrubs, herbaceous) or By plant characteristic, such as Pollinator-attracting or Soil-binding. Tick the plants you want, search to find more, then click Add selected.
  2. Add custom circle — places a new circle on the plan. Set its labels, size, color and pattern in Selected circle, then click Save to plant menu.
  3. Upload CSV — load a whole plant list from a spreadsheet. Download the example CSV in that window to see the columns it needs.

Each plant gets its own color and pattern automatically, so no two look alike. To reorder the menu, drag a plant up or down within its category, or drag a category heading. Save plant list keeps the whole menu so you can load it again from Presets.

Step 3: Arrange the spacing diagram

Click a plant in your menu to place it on the block plan. Each plant appears as a circle as wide as the average space it needs when grown, so circles that just touch are correctly spaced. These are all just defaults — look up each plant's specific needs to know whether you can cram them together (like we do with snowberry) or give them a wide berth.

  • Move: drag a circle. Hold Shift to snap it to the grid.
  • Nudge: select a circle and use the arrow keys (Shift moves a full grid square).
  • Remove: select a circle and press Delete.
  • Edit: the Selected circle panel changes its labels, diameter, color, pattern and layer. Update saved plant applies the change to every copy of that plant.
  • Layers: use the Layers menu to fade layers you aren't working on, for example to place shrubs around trees.

Undo and Redo step back and forward through your changes.

Step 4: Switch to the planting diagram

Click Planting diagram in the View toggle to turn the circles into symbols, one per plant, at the center of each circle. This is the plan to take into the field: each symbol marks where a plant goes in the ground.

Below the plan, the key lists every plant by layer with a count of how many you've placed. In the spacing diagram the count sits inside each color swatch; in the planting diagram it follows the plant's name. Click Spacing diagram to go back; your arrangement doesn't change.

Step 5: Save, share and export

The planner saves your work in your browser automatically. To keep versions or move your work, use these:

To do thisUseWhere
Keep a version of this block to come back to in this browserName it, then SaveSaved layouts
Start from a ready-made planLoad “Top Picks” for close to homeSaved layouts
Back up everything, or move it to another computerSave plan file, then Open plan fileSaved layouts
Print or share the diagramPNG or PDF, with an optional title and notesMore options

Loading a layout offers to add its plants to your menu, so you can place more of them. Exports include the key, and can include a scale bar and a compass pointing north.

Tips and troubleshooting

  • My plan disappeared. Work is saved in the browser you used. Clearing browsing data or switching browsers or computers starts fresh, so save a plan file as a backup.
  • Two plants look the same. The planner warns you about this. Change one plant's color or pattern in Selected circle, then click Update saved plant.
  • I want common names in the key. Turn on Show common names in key under More options → Display options.
  • Delete didn't remove a circle. Click the circle first so it's selected, then press Delete.
  • Something isn't working, or I have an idea. Use About → Feedback, or email cameron@nativeplantsalvage.org.

When designing your hedgerow, start with circles to represent the spacing for each type/size of plant (e.g. small shrubs vs. trees) rather than the size of the plants themselves. Using the recommended spacing, the center of one tree (large, orange circles here) should be 10 feet from the center of another tree. When laying out large shrubs (medium, purple circles) in the same way, those circles should not overlap one another, but can fill in and overlap the trees’ spacing.

The spacing recommendations ensure the center of each plant is a certain distance from another—the actual plants you choose might be larger or smaller than their spacing circles.

When you drop in the actual widths of your chosen plants (we suggest using the height and width of the plant at at least around 8 years maturity), do so from the largest category to smallest in order to get a sense of what will fit. Remember, two trees spaced 10 feet apart might not require the same amount of space underneath. One could be bushy and wide near the ground, the other could have a narrow trunk and a 20-foot spread in the canopy, which will change the plants you choose to place around and under it.

Upload a CSV to fill the plant menu

Your file needs a header row with these five column names, in any order (capitalization doesn’t matter):

ColumnWhat to enter
Menu labelThe longer name shown in the plant menu
Display labelThe name shown on the circle. To use a second line, type | where it should break (for example PIN|CON), or put a real line break inside quotes.
Text sizeA number, or leave blank to auto-size to the circle
DiameterSpacing circle diameter in feet, such as 6 or 2.5
LayerTrees, Large shrubs, Small shrubs, Herbaceous, or the name of a layer you created

Colors and patterns are assigned automatically, and you can change them after adding a plant to the block plan. Plants are added to your current menu. Rows with a missing or invalid diameter or layer are skipped.

Menu label,Display label,Text size,Diameter,Layer
Shore Pine,PIN|CON,,10,Trees
Snowberry (deciduous with berries),Snowberry,12,4,Small shrubs

About

The Native Plant Salvage Project was started in 1994 to involve Thurston County residents in direct action to protect water resources and improve habitat. Our mission is to provide hands-on education to protect and conserve water resources and habitat from the South Sound prairies to the shores of the Salish Sea.

What’s new and what’s changed in the planner, newest first.

November 9, 2026 update

  • featureTips & Templates has a new “How to use this planner” guide, with step-by-step instructions and screenshots.
  • featureYou can now drag plants to reorder them within a category in the Add a plant menu, and drag category headings to reorder the categories.
  • featureSaved layouts now include “Top Picks” for close to home, a ready-made layout from the Native Plant Salvage Foundation you can load and adapt.
  • fixedIn Presets, plants you checked while searching for one name were dropped when you searched for another. Now every plant you check is added.
  • featureThe View dropdown is now a toggle, so you can switch between the spacing and planting diagrams with one click.

November 7, 2026 update

  • fixedPressing Delete sometimes didn’t remove the selected circle after you’d been editing a label or ticking a setting.
  • featureIn the spacing diagram, the key now shows how many of each plant are on the block plan inside its color swatch, and the swatches use a finer pattern so dots and stripes are easy to see. The planting diagram key still shows the count after the name.
  • featureMore options has a new Display options group with a “Show common names in key” switch. It’s off to start, so the key lists plants by scientific name; turn it on to include common names.
  • featurePresets now has a “By plant characteristic” section under the Native Plant Salvage Foundation, with lists such as Pollinator-attracting, Larval hosts and Soil-binding, so you can pick plants by what they do in a hedgerow.
  • featureLoading a saved layout now offers to add any of its plants that aren’t in your Add a plant menu, so you can place more of them and update them later.
